summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science education. In discrete mathematics they have sets, counting and binomial coefficients, induction, graphs, modular arithmetic, gcd and the extended Euclidean algorithm, primes and the Chinese remainder theorem. In algorithms and theory they have worst-case analysis, recurrences, sorting, stacks, binary counters, schoolbook and Karatsuba multiplication, Boolean circuits and the multitape Turing machine with its constant-factor simulations, and in computer arithmetic they have binary, two's-complement and fixed-point numbers with carries. They have also taken a first course in linear algebra over the reals (vector spaces, matrices, Gaussian elimination, triangular matrices, eigenvalues, dot products, projections) and calculus (limits, series, exponentials, Newton's method), plus complex numbers with Euler's formula. They have not studied bilinear forms over finite fields, tensor products, ring theory beyond the integers mod n, Fourier analysis or FFT internals, numerical error analysis, or the integer-multiplication literature after Karatsuba.

known.name: Binary representation of integers
known.gloss: Writing a nonnegative integer as a string of bits, each weighted by a power of two, where padding on the left with zeroes does not change the value.

known.name: Logarithms
known.gloss: The inverse of exponentiation, with log₂ n roughly the number of bits of n, and with the usual laws for products, powers and change of base.

known.name: Floor and ceiling functions
known.gloss: The functions ⌊x⌋ and ⌈x⌉ giving the largest integer not above x and the smallest integer not below x.

known.name: Two's complement
known.gloss: The standard fixed-width encoding of signed integers in which a w-bit word represents values from −2^{w−1} to 2^{w−1}−1 and addition is ordinary binary addition modulo 2^w.

known.name: Fixed-point binary numbers
known.gloss: Numbers stored as an integer times a fixed power of two 2^{−p}, so addition, subtraction and multiplication or division by powers of two are exact integer operations with a shifted binary point.

known.name: Schoolbook binary arithmetic and carry propagation
known.gloss: The digit-by-digit algorithms for adding, subtracting and multiplying binary numbers, in which carries move from less to more significant positions and multiplication takes quadratic time.

known.name: Integer division with remainder
known.gloss: For integers a ≥ 0 and b > 0, the unique q = ⌊a/b⌋ and r = a − bq with 0 ≤ r < b, and similarly ⌊√a⌋ as the largest integer whose square is at most a.

known.name: Modular arithmetic
known.gloss: Arithmetic on integers up to multiples of a modulus Q, where a ≡ b (mod Q) means Q divides a − b, and an integer coprime to Q has a multiplicative inverse modulo Q.

known.name: Greatest common divisor and the extended Euclidean algorithm
known.gloss: The largest integer dividing two given integers, computed by repeated division with remainder, whose extended form also finds x, y with ax + by = gcd(a, b) and hence modular inverses.

known.name: Prime numbers
known.gloss: Integers greater than one whose only positive divisors are one and themselves, so every integer not divisible by a prime p is invertible modulo p.

known.name: Chinese remainder theorem
known.gloss: For pairwise coprime moduli s₁, …, s_d, the residue of an integer modulo their product corresponds one-to-one to its tuple of residues modulo each sᵢ, compatibly with addition and multiplication.

known.name: Sets, Cartesian products and indicator vectors
known.gloss: Basic set operations and sizes, the set of tuples A₁ × ⋯ × A_t, and the 0/1 vector recording which elements of a ground set belong to a subset.

known.name: Binomial coefficients
known.gloss: The number C(n, k) = n!/(k!(n−k)!) of k-element subsets of an n-element set, used to count subsets and pairs with given intersections.

known.name: Permutations and bijections
known.gloss: Invertible maps from a finite set onto itself (or between two sets), which can be composed and inverted and which rearrange the entries of an indexed array.

known.name: Mathematical induction
known.gloss: Proving a statement for all natural numbers by checking a base case and showing each case follows from the previous ones.

known.name: Directed graphs
aliases: head and tail of an edge
known.gloss: A set of vertices with edges, each directed from a tail vertex to a head vertex, along which paths and orderings can be traced.

known.name: Worst-case running time
known.gloss: The maximum number of steps a deterministic algorithm takes over all inputs of a given size, studied as a function of that size.

known.name: RAM model of computation
known.gloss: A machine model with directly addressable memory in which reading or writing any word and basic arithmetic on words count as one step each, unlike a tape machine.

known.name: Recurrence relations and divide and conquer
known.gloss: Expressing an algorithm's cost on size n through its costs on smaller subproblems, as in T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n), and solving for its asymptotic growth.

known.name: Geometric series
known.gloss: Sums a + ar + ar² + ⋯ with ratio r, which for |r| < 1 stay within a constant factor of their largest term.

known.name: Karatsuba multiplication
known.gloss: The recursive algorithm that multiplies two n-digit numbers with three half-size products instead of four, giving O(n^{log₂ 3}) time.

known.name: Polynomial evaluation and interpolation
known.gloss: A polynomial of degree below k is determined by its values at k distinct points, so polynomials can be multiplied by evaluating, multiplying values pointwise and interpolating back.

known.name: Sorting
known.gloss: Rearranging records into increasing order of a key, which takes O(n log n) comparisons in general and can be done by sequential merging on tapes.

known.name: Stacks
known.gloss: A last-in first-out store in which items are pushed and popped at one end, so popping returns them in reverse order.

known.name: Binary counters
known.gloss: A binary number repeatedly incremented by one, where L consecutive increments flip O(L + width) bits in total because bit j changes only once every 2^j counts.

known.name: Matrix transposition and row-major order
known.gloss: Storing an n₁ × n₂ matrix row after row, so entry (i, j) is at position n₂i + j, and transposing it moves that entry to position n₁j + i.

known.name: Vector spaces, subspaces and dimension
known.gloss: Sets of vectors closed under addition and scalar multiplication over a field, with subspaces, spans, bases and the dimension as the size of any basis.

known.name: Matrices and linear maps
known.gloss: Rectangular arrays representing linear maps between coordinate spaces, composed by matrix multiplication and inverted when they are bijective, including identity, diagonal and permutation matrices.

known.name: Gaussian elimination and triangular matrices
known.gloss: Reducing a matrix by elementary row and column operations around pivot entries, where lower triangular matrices have zeros above the diagonal, are closed under products and inverses, and are invertible when their diagonal is nonzero.

known.name: Eigenvalues
known.gloss: Scalars λ with Av = λv for a nonzero vector v, so a symmetric matrix is invertible exactly when none of its eigenvalues is zero.

known.name: Dot product and orthonormal bases
known.gloss: The product x·y = Σ xᵢyᵢ, in which vectors are orthogonal when it is zero, and an orthonormal basis consists of pairwise orthogonal vectors each of product one with itself.

known.name: Projections onto subspaces
known.gloss: The linear map that writes a vector as a sum of a part in a subspace U and a part in a complementary subspace and keeps only the U part; it satisfies P² = P and has rank dim U.

known.name: Direct sums
known.gloss: Combining spaces or operators side by side, so that V = U ⊕ U′ means each vector splits uniquely into parts from U and U′, and ⊕ of operators acts on each block separately.

known.name: Hamming weight
known.gloss: The number of nonzero coordinates of a binary vector, whose parity is the vector's sum over F₂.

known.name: Euler's formula and the complex exponential
known.gloss: The identity e^{iθ} = cos θ + i sin θ, which makes e^{2πij/k} the k-th roots of unity and turns multiplication by unit-modulus numbers into rotations.

known.name: Exponential function and Gaussian function
known.gloss: The function e^x and the rapidly decaying bell-shaped function e^{−πx²} built from it.

known.name: Limits and convergent series
known.gloss: The limiting value of a sequence or of the partial sums of a series, where absolute convergence lets the terms be summed in any order.

known.name: Triangle inequality
known.gloss: The inequality |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b| for real or complex numbers, used to add error bounds from separate steps.

known.name: Newton's method
known.gloss: The iteration that refines an approximate root of an equation by linearizing it, roughly doubling the number of correct digits at each step, as in x ← x(2 − cx) for 1/c.
